topics.name: Period study AA America, 1840–1895: Expansion and consolidation
points: The geography of North America: views of the Great American Desert; belief in Manifest Destiny
Why the early settlers went west: Brigham Young and the Mormons, pioneer farmers, the journey west, miners
Dealing with a different culture: Plains Indian lifestyle, early government policy, Permanent Indian Frontier
Increasing conflict on the Plains: Fort Laramie Treaty 1851, Indian Wars 1862–67, Sand Creek, Fetterman's Trap
The background to the American Civil War: slavery, westward expansion, abolitionism, Missouri Compromise, John Brown, Lincoln and Davis
Coming to terms with the Mormons: Mountain Meadow Massacre and its aftermath
The aftermath of the Civil War: 13th Amendment, Civil Rights Act, Southern Reconstruction 1866–77, Federal and State powers
The continued settlement of the west: homesteaders, government laws, railroads, farming problems and solutions
The resolution of 'the Indian problem' after 1865: reservations, Little Big Horn, Dawes Act, Wounded Knee, closing of the frontier

topics.name: Period study AB Germany, 1890–1945: Democracy and dictatorship
points: Kaiser Wilhelm and the difficulties of ruling Germany: parliament, Prussian militarism, industrialisation, socialism, Navy Laws
Impact of the First World War: war weariness, defeat, end of monarchy, reparations, Ruhr occupation, hyperinflation
Weimar democracy: unrest 1919–23 (Spartacists, Kapp Putsch, Munich Putsch), Stresemann, Dawes and Young Plans, Weimar culture
The impact of the Depression: growth of support for the Nazis and extremist parties 1928–32, the SA, Hitler's appeal
The failure of Weimar democracy: election results, Papen and Hindenburg, Hitler's appointment as Chancellor
The establishment of Hitler's dictatorship: Reichstag Fire, Enabling Act, Night of the Long Knives, Hitler as Führer
Economic changes: employment, public works, rearmament, self-sufficiency; impact of war on the economy and people
Social policy and practice: women, young people, education, churches, Aryan ideas, racial persecution, the Final Solution
Control: Goebbels, propaganda and censorship, Nazi culture, the police state (SS, Gestapo), resistance and the July 1944 plot

topics.name: Period study AC Russia, 1894–1945: Tsardom and communism
points: Russia's economy and society: industrialisation; living and working conditions in towns and the countryside
Nicholas II's autocracy and the court: opposition, 1905 Revolution and October Manifesto, Dumas, Stolypin
The First World War: military defeats, social and economic effects, Rasputin, the Tsar's abdication
The Provisional Government: its failures, Lenin and Trotsky, growth of Bolshevik support, the October/November Revolution
The impact of Lenin's dictatorship: ending the war, the Cheka, the Red Army, the Civil War, propaganda
Social and economic developments: War Communism, Kronstadt Rising, New Economic Policy, achievements of Lenin and Trotsky
Stalin the dictator: struggle for power, Terror and Purges, secret police, labour camps, censorship, cult of personality
Stalin's modernisation of the USSR: collectivisation, Five Year Plans, effects on kulaks, workers and women
Impact of the Second World War: Stalin's wartime leadership; political, economic and social problems up to 1945

topics.name: Period study AD America, 1920–1973: Opportunity and inequality
points: The 'Boom': consumerism, advertising, hire purchase, mass production, Republican policies, stock market boom, inequality of wealth
Social and cultural developments: cinema, jazz, the position of women including flappers
Divided society: Prohibition and organised crime, immigration, racial tension, Ku Klux Klan, Red Scare, Sacco and Vanzetti
American society during the Depression: unemployment, farmers, businessmen, Hoover's unpopularity, Roosevelt's election
The effectiveness of the New Deal on different groups: successes and limits, opposition including the Supreme Court, Roosevelt's role
The impact of the Second World War: economic recovery, Lend Lease, experiences of African-Americans and women
Post-war American society and economy: consumerism, the American Dream, McCarthyism, Rock and Roll, television
Racial tension and Civil Rights campaigns in the 1950s and 1960s: segregation, Martin Luther King, Malcolm X, Black Power, Civil Rights Acts 1964 and 1968
America and the 'Great Society': Kennedy and Johnson's social policies, feminist movements, NOW, Roe v Wade, Equal Rights Amendment

topics.name: Wider world depth study BA Conflict and tension: The First World War, 1894–1918
points: The Alliance System: Triple Alliance, Franco-Russian Alliance, Entente, Moroccan and Balkan crises
Anglo-German rivalry: end of Splendid Isolation, Kaiser Wilhelm's Weltpolitik, colonial rivalry, the naval race
Outbreak of war: Slav nationalism, Serbia and Austria-Hungary, Sarajevo assassination, July Crisis, Schlieffen Plan and Belgium
The Schlieffen Plan: reasons for it, failure at the Marne, contribution to stalemate
The Western Front: trench warfare and technology, attrition, Verdun, the Somme, Passchendaele
The wider war: Gallipoli; war at sea including Jutland, U-boats and convoys
Changes in the Allied Forces: Russian withdrawal after the Bolshevik Revolution; US entry into the war
Military developments in 1918: new tactics and technology, Ludendorff's Spring Offensive, the Hundred Days
Germany surrenders: the blockade, the Kaiser's abdication, the armistice, roles of Haig and Foch

topics.name: Wider world depth study BB Conflict and tension: The inter-war years, 1918–1939
points: The armistice: aims of the peacemakers, Wilson's Fourteen Points, Clemenceau and Lloyd George
The Versailles Settlement: Diktat, territorial changes, military restrictions, war guilt and reparations
Impact of the treaty and wider settlement: reactions of the Allies and Germany, strengths and weaknesses, new states
The League of Nations: covenant, organisation, membership, powers, agencies; successes and failures in the 1920s
Diplomacy outside the League: Locarno treaties, Kellogg-Briand Pact
The collapse of the League: effects of the Depression, Manchurian and Abyssinian crises
The development of tension: Hitler's aims, Dollfuss Affair, Saar, rearmament, Stresa Front, Anglo-German Naval Agreement
Escalation of tension: Rhineland, Anschluss, appeasement, Sudeten Crisis and Munich
The outbreak of war: occupation of Czechoslovakia, Nazi-Soviet Pact, invasion of Poland; responsibility of Hitler, Stalin, Chamberlain

topics.name: Wider world depth study BC Conflict and tension between East and West, 1945–1972
points: The end of the Second World War: Yalta and Potsdam, division of Germany, rival ideologies, impact of the atom bomb
The Iron Curtain and East-West rivalry: Soviet expansion, Truman Doctrine, Marshall Plan, Cominform, Comecon, Berlin Blockade and Airlift
The significance of events in Asia: Mao, the Korean War, the Vietcong against France and the USA
Military rivalries: the arms race, NATO and the Warsaw Pact, the space race
The 'Thaw': Hungary and Nagy, U2 Crisis and the Paris Summit
Berlin Wall: reasons for its construction and Kennedy's response
Tensions over Cuba: Castro, Bay of Pigs, the Cuban Missile Crisis, roles of Khrushchev and Kennedy
Czechoslovakia: Dubček and the Prague Spring, the Soviet response, the Brezhnev Doctrine
Easing of tension: reasons for Détente and SALT 1, roles of Brezhnev and Nixon

topics.name: Wider world depth study BD Conflict and tension in Asia, 1950–1975
points: The causes of the Korean War: division of Korea, Kim Il Sung and Rhee, North's invasion, UN and USSR responses
The development of the Korean War: UN campaigns, Inchon, Chinese intervention, MacArthur's dismissal
The end of the Korean War: stalemate at the 38th Parallel, armistice, impact on Korea, the UN and Sino-American relations
The end of French colonial rule: Dien Bien Phu, Geneva Agreement 1954, Diem, Ho Chi Minh and the Vietcong
The US involvement: Domino Theory, Eisenhower and Kennedy, Strategic Hamlets
Johnson's War: Gulf of Tonkin, bombing, Search and Destroy, My Lai, Tet Offensive, student protests
Nixon's War: Vietnamisation, chemical warfare, bombing 1970–72, relations with China, Laos and Cambodia
Opposition to war: Kent State, the media and television, Watergate
The end of the war: Paris Peace talks, Kissinger, US withdrawal, fall of Saigon, costs of the war

topics.name: Wider world depth study BE Conflict and tension in the Gulf and Afghanistan, 1990–2009
points: Regional instability: Iran-Iraq War, Western and Russian interests, oil, Israeli-Palestinian conflict and terrorism
The Gulf War, 1990: Iraqi invasion of Kuwait, Bush and Thatcher, UN campaign, consequences and Arab reactions
Al-Qaeda: aims, Osama bin Laden, the 11 September attacks
Afghanistan: the Taliban regime, Western and Muslim attitudes, ethnic divisions, Taliban resurgence
Bush's war against terror: Bush's aims, Blair's support, 2001 operation, overthrow of the Taliban, Karzai's problems
Saddam Hussein's regime: treatment of Kurds and Shia, Al-Qaeda links debate, international attitudes, UN role
The invasion of Iraq 2003: weapons inspectors and WMD, the military campaign, opposition, Saddam's downfall
The impact of war on Iraq and the world: insurgency, elections, terrorism against the US and UK, 2007 surge, stability by 2009

topics.name: Thematic study AA Britain: Health and the people: c1000 to the present day
points: Medieval medicine: natural and supernatural ideas, Hippocrates and Galen, medieval doctors and beliefs about causes of illness
Medical progress: contribution of Christianity, hospitals, Islamic medicine and surgery, medieval surgery
Public health in the Middle Ages: towns and monasteries, the Black Death in Britain
The impact of the Renaissance on Britain: challenges to authority, Vesalius, Paré and Harvey
Dealing with disease: traditional and new treatments, the Great Plague, hospitals, surgeons, John Hunter
Prevention of disease: inoculation, Edward Jenner and vaccination, opposition to change
The development of Germ Theory and its impact: Pasteur, Koch, Ehrlich's magic bullets
A revolution in surgery: anaesthetics (Simpson, chloroform), antiseptics (Lister, carbolic acid), aseptic surgery
Improvements in public health: industrial towns, cholera, reformers, Public Health Acts 1848 and 1875
Modern treatment of disease: pharmaceutical industry, Fleming and penicillin, new diseases, antibiotic resistance, alternative treatments
The impact of war and technology on surgery: plastic surgery, blood transfusions, X-rays, transplants, keyhole surgery
Modern public health: Booth, Rowntree, Boer War, Liberal reforms, Beveridge Report, the NHS, 21st-century issues

topics.name: Thematic study AB Britain: Power and the people: c1170 to the present day
points: Constraints on kingship: King John and the barons, Magna Carta and its impact
The origins of parliament: Henry III, Simon de Montfort, Provisions of Oxford, Parliament of 1265
Medieval revolt and royal authority: the Peasants' Revolt, its causes, events and impact
Popular uprisings against the Crown: the Pilgrimage of Grace and Henry VIII's reaction
Divine Right and parliamentary authority: the English Revolution, New Model Army, radicalism, trial of Charles I
Royal authority and the right to representation: the American Revolution and its significance
The extension of the franchise: radical protest, the Great Reform Act, Chartism
Protest and change: the Anti-Slavery movement, Anti-Corn Law League, factory and social reformers
Workers' movements: Tolpuddle Martyrs, New Model Unions, new unionism, match girls' and dockers' strikes
Women's rights: the suffrage campaign, the Pankhursts, extension of the franchise, later 20th-century progress
Workers' rights: the General Strike 1926, trade union reform in the late 20th century
Minority rights: multi-racial society since 1945, discrimination, protest and reform, Brixton Riots, Scarman Report

topics.name: Thematic study AC Britain: Migration, empires and the people: c790 to the present day
points: Invasion: Vikings and Anglo-Saxons, Danelaw, Alfred and Wessex, Cnut and the North Sea Empire
A Norman Kingdom and 'Angevin' Empire: Henry II, invasion of Ireland, losses under John
The birth of English identity: the Hundred Years' War and its impact
Sugar and the Caribbean: piracy, the slave trade including Hawkins, Caribbean settlements, impact on Britain
Colonisation in North America: Raleigh, Jamestown, Pilgrim Fathers, loss of the American colonies
Migrants to and from Britain: Huguenots, Highland clearances, Ulster plantations
Expansion in India: East India Company, Clive, Hastings, the Indian Rebellion of 1857
Expansion in Africa: trade and missionaries, Egypt, the Scramble for Africa, Rhodes, Boer War, imperial propaganda
Migrants to, from and within Britain: Irish and Jewish migration, transportation, migration within the Empire
The end of Empire: impact of the World Wars, Suez, independence in India and Africa, Gandhi, Nkrumah, Kenyatta
The legacy of Empire: Windrush, Claudia Jones, migration from Asia and Africa, the Commonwealth, Falklands War
Britain's relationship with Europe and its impact: EU membership, end of the Cold War, migration

topics.name: British depth study BA Norman England, c1066–c1100
points: Causes of the Norman Conquest: death of Edward the Confessor, the claimants and their claims
Military aspects: Stamford Bridge, Hastings, Anglo-Saxon and Norman tactics, castles
Establishing and maintaining control: revolts 1067–75, Harrying of the North, William I's government, William II
Feudalism and government: landholding, lordship, military service, justice, the Domesday Book
Economic and social changes: towns, villages, work, seasonal life, Forest law
The Church: Lanfranc's reforms, Church courts, Church and state, Investiture Controversy
Monasticism: Norman reforms, abbeys and monastic life, learning and schools
The historic environment of Norman England: the specified site, its location, function, structure, people and links to events

topics.name: British depth study BB Medieval England: the reign of Edward I, 1272–1307
points: Henry III's legacy: problems on Edward's accession, relations with the nobility, Edward's character
Development of government, rights and justice: Hundred Rolls, Statutes of Westminster and Mortmain, Quo Warranto, Model Parliament 1295
Trade, towns and villages: wool trade and taxation, royal finance, Italian bankers, re-coinage, expulsion of the Jews 1290
Education and learning: the Church, universities, Roger Bacon, Duns Scotus
The development of the legal system: courts, crime and punishment, Statutes of Gloucester and Winchester
Medieval warfare, tactics and technology: siege warfare, cavalry, infantry, weapons and armour
The invasion and colonisation of Wales: Welsh Wars, Statute of Rhuddlan, castle building
The relations with Scotland: the Great Cause, Balliol, Wallace, Bruce, First War of Scottish Independence
The historic environment of Medieval England: the specified site, its location, function, structure, people and links to events

topics.name: British depth study BC Elizabethan England, c1568–1603
points: Elizabeth I and her court: background and character, court life, patronage, key ministers
The difficulties of a female ruler: Parliament, marriage and succession, Essex's rebellion 1601
A 'Golden Age': living standards, fashions, the gentry, the theatre
The poor: reasons for poverty, attitudes and responses, government action
English sailors: Hawkins, Drake and the circumnavigation 1577–80, voyages and trade, Raleigh
Religious matters: Catholics and Puritans, Northern Rebellion, excommunication, missionaries, plots, government responses
Mary Queen of Scots: background, plots, execution and its impact
Conflict with Spain: reasons, naval tactics and technology, defeat of the Spanish Armada
The historic environment of Elizabethan England: the specified site, its location, function, structure, people and links to events

topics.name: British depth study BD Restoration England, 1660–1685
points: Crown and Parliament: legacy of the Civil War, the Restoration settlement, finance and religion, the Cabal, rule without Parliament from 1681
The Catholic question: Popish Plot, Exclusion Bill 1679, Rye House Plot, James, Duke of York
Charles II's court: Charles's character, court life and fashions
Crisis: the Great Plague 1665 and Fire of London 1666, responses and rebuilding
Restoration culture: theatres and playwrights, coffee houses, the Royal Society, Pepys, Wren
Land: East India Company, Bombay, Hudson Bay, Tangier, Morgan and Jamaica
Trade: mercantilism, Navigation Acts, the slave trade
War: English sea power, Second and Third Dutch Wars, relations with Spain and France
The historic environment of Restoration England: the specified site, its location, function, structure, people and links to events
